definitions.explanation: The opening in the face used for eating and speaking.

examples.japanese: {口|くち}を{開|あ}けてください。
この{料理|りょうり}は{口|くち}に{合|あ}いますか？
examples.english: Does this dish suit your taste?
examples.notes: 口に合う = to suit one's taste

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{口|くち}が{堅|かた}い{人|ひと}なので、{秘密|ひみつ}を{話|はな}しても{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です。
examples.english: He is a person who can keep secrets, so it's okay to tell him secrets.

examples.japanese: {走|はし}った{後|あと}は{口|くち}の{中|なか}が{乾|かわ}いて{喉|のど}も{渇|かわ}くので、{水|みず}をたくさん{飲|の}みます。
examples.english: After running, my mouth gets dry and I get thirsty, so I drink a lot of water.

examples.japanese: {食|た}べながら{話|はな}すと{口|くち}の{中|なか}の{物|もの}が{見|み}えてしまうので、{口|くち}の{中|なか}の{食|た}べ{物|もの}を{飲|の}み{込|こ}んでから{話|はな}しましょう。
examples.english: When you talk while eating, people can see the food in your mouth, so let's swallow the food before talking.

notes:
IDIOMATIC EXPRESSIONS:
- {口|くち}に{合|あ}う: to suit one's taste
- {口|くち}が{堅|かた}い: tight-lipped, discreet
- {口|くち}が{軽|かる}い: loose-lipped, indiscreet
- {口|くち}を{出|だ}す: to interfere, butt in
- {口|くち}を{聞|き}く: to speak, to mediate

EXTENDED MEANINGS:
{口|くち} also means "opening" and appears in many compound words:
- {入|い}り{口|ぐち}: entrance
- {出|で}{口|ぐち}: exit
- {窓口|まどぐち}: service window, counter
- {改札口|かいさつぐち}: ticket gate

Note: Reading changes to ぐち in compounds.
